extracted.intended_audience: educational institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, legal/compliance staff at recipients of Federal education funds
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for recipients' notice, publication, reporting, and grievance procedures under Title IX, including special rules for formal complaints of sexual harassment and religious exemptions. Useful for institutions drafting or revising policies and procedures to comply with §§106.8–106.12 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication of non-discrimination policy (§106.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish a non-discrimination policy so relevant persons and organizations know the recipient's non-discrimination policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will not prescribe how a recipient must organize its website (e.g., policy may be placed on multiple specific pages, as a PDF link, in multiple languages), but §106.8 sets reasonable, enforceable requirements to ensure awareness. The policy must state that the requirement not to discriminate extends to admission “unless subpart C of this part does not apply,” and the final regulations use the phrase “permitted by title IX or this part” to reference statutory and regulatory exemptions. Nothing in §106.8 exempts the policy from laws/regulations requiring translation into other languages. Recipients may also state on their website or publications that they have particular statutory or regulatory exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and publish grievance procedures for prompt and equitable resolution (§106.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of student and employee complaints alleging any action prohibited by Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify recipients must have 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures for sex discrimination generally. The Department expects recipients to disseminate how to report and file complaints and how the recipient will respond. The Department will enforce the requirement that recipients adopt and publish grievance procedures and designate a Title IX Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process that complies with §106.45 for formal complaints of sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must have and publish a grievance process that complies with §106.45 specifically for formal complaints of sexual harassment (as defined in §106.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The §106.45 grievance process is a prescribed process designed to increase legitimacy and reliability of determinations and reduce bias; recipients may choose to apply §106.45 to non-sexual-harassment complaints but are only required to use it for formal sexual-harassment complaints. Recipients are precluded from imposing disciplinary sanctions on a respondent without first following a §106.45-compliant grievance process for a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any person may report sexual harassment and reports may be made at any time (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (whether or not the person reporting is the person alleged to be victimized) may report sexual harassment using the contact information listed for the Title IX Coordinator, at any time including during non-business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may be made by telephone, email, or mail to the office address listed for the Title IX Coordinator. The §106.30 definition of 'actual knowledge' explicitly includes such reports to the Title IX Coordinator, and the Department revised §106.8(a) and §106.30 to emphasize these points. Accessible reporting channels and the right of any person to report are permitted and do not constitute a prohibition on recipients communicating prevention efforts (e.g., bystander intervention, flyers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between third-party notice and formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient can obtain actual knowledge of sexual harassment via third-party reporting, but a third party may not file a 'formal complaint' as defined in §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'formal complaint' must be filed by a complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator. Third-party reports can trigger the recipient's obligations to respond (e.g., supportive measures) but do not substitute for the formal-complaint filing requirement that triggers §106.45 adjudication unless the Title IX Coordinator signs a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and permissible methods for filing a formal complaint (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'formal complaint' of sexual harassment is defined as a document signed by a complainant; it may be filed in person, by mail, by email, or by any other method designated by the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may provide a specific form or online portal for filing, but a complainant may instead file by physically or digitally signing any document and submitting it by the allowed methods. The final regulations permit flexibility in submission methods so complainants are not constrained to a single form if they provide a signed document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice recipients and required content of notice about grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must send notice of the 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures and the §106.45 grievance process to students, employees, applicants for admission and employment, parents/legal guardians of elementary and secondary students, unions and similar professional organizations, and persons entitled to notice under §106.8(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must include how to report or file a complaint of sex discrimination, how to report or file a formal complaint of sexual harassment, and how the recipient will respond. The revisions expand the list of persons who must receive such notice to ensure wider awareness of procedures and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of retaliation complaints (§106.71(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints of retaliation for exercise of rights under Title IX must be handled under the 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures referenced in §106.8(c) (i.e., treated like non-sexual-harassment sex discrimination complaints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified in §106.71(a) that retaliation complaints are subject to the 'prompt and equitable' procedures rather than the §106.45 formal-complaint sexual-harassment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification when grievance procedures/processes change
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient no longer uses one grievance procedure or process and uses a different procedure or process, the recipient must publish and send notice of the change to the relevant groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The obligation to 'adopt and publish' requires recipients to inform their educational community of how to report sex discrimination or sexual harassment, how to file complaints, and how the recipient will respond. The Department notes some recipients historically failed to adopt and publish such procedures and intends to enforce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application outside the United States (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of paragraph (c) (non-discrimination policy, grievance procedures, and grievance process) apply only to sex discrimination occurring against a person in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded Title IX lacks extraterritorial application based on statutory text and judicial canons. Recipients remain free to adopt anti-harassment and disciplinary policies that apply to programs or activities located abroad and may offer supportive measures for misconduct occurring overseas, but the Title IX regulatory obligations do not extend to persons outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious-organization-controlled institutions and Title IX exemptions (§106.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: An educational institution controlled by a religious organization is not subject to Title IX to the extent that application of Title IX would be inconsistent with the organization's religious tenets; recipients may invoke religious exemptions without previously obtaining an assurance letter from OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations codify OCR practice that a recipient can invoke a religious exemption even after OCR has received a complaint; however, the recipient must invoke and establish eligibility for the exemption (the final regulations do not shift the burden to the government to disprove exemptions). OCR will still respond to requests for assurance letters as an option for schools that wish to obtain one preemptively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and language-access obligations are not excused by §106.8
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no exemption for a recipient's §106.8-required non-discrimination policy from laws, regulations, Federal standards, and recipient policies requiring translation of materials into languages other than English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Department permits recipients to choose how to present the policy (multiple pages, PDFs, multiple languages), recipients must still comply with applicable translation and language-access obligations under other authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department response to commenter suggestions (providing complaint forms, parental involvement, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested specific practices (e.g., requiring elementary and secondary schools to provide copies of complaint forms, involving parents/student groups in policy drafting, mandating acknowledgements, timelines for acknowledging complaints, independent review boards), but the Department's final regulations clarify existing requirements and allow but do not require many of these specific practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department responded that while recipients may adopt suggested practices (making complaint forms publicly available, involving parent/student groups, providing curricula, training), the final regulations focus on requiring adoption and publication of grievance procedures and a §106.45-compliant process for formal sexual-harassment complaints rather than imposing the detailed procedural architecture some commenters requested. The Department explained how aspects such as acknowledging complaints, independent review boards, and specific timelines are matters recipients may implement consistent with §106.8 and §106.45, but they are not mandated in the final regulation text excerpted here.
